keyVerseText: The children of Solomon's servants: the children of Sotai, the children of Sophereth, the children of Peruda, Peruda: or, Perida
rootMeaning: The root of פְּרוּדָא (Pᵉrûwdâʼ) is פָּרַד (pârad), which means to disperse, divide, or separate. This etymology suggests a foundational idea of separation or scattering, which goes beyond a mere proper name and hints at a historical or familial dispersion. The literal sense of division or scattering enriches our understanding of the name as possibly denoting a lineage or group that was once separated or scattered, fitting the context of post-exilic restoration.
usageInScripture: This word appears only twice in Scripture, both times as a proper name connected to a family or group associated with Solomon's servants who returned from exile. It is translated as 'Peruda' or 'Perida,' showing some variation but consistently indicating a specific ancestral name. The limited occurrences and consistent use as a proper name highlight its role in identifying a particular lineage among temple servants rather than a common noun or concept.
theologicalSignificance: The name פְּרוּדָא, rooted in the concept of dispersion, reminds believers of God's providential care in gathering and restoring His people after exile and separation. It underscores the faithfulness of God in preserving distinct families and servant lineages for His purposes, demonstrating His sovereignty over history and human divisions. For the Christian faith, this reflects the greater spiritual truth of Christ gathering His scattered people into one body, overcoming division and separation through redemption. Recognizing the historical and linguistic background of such names enriches our appreciation of God's faithfulness to His covenant community.
keyVerseReflection: Ezra 2:55 lists 'the children of Peruda' among the descendants of Solomon's servants who returned from exile with Zerubbabel. The use of this name here emphasizes the continuity and restoration of God's people, even those who were once scattered or separated. The word 'Peruda' in this verse connects the narrative of return and rebuilding to the theme of divine preservation amid dispersion, highlighting God's ongoing work to reunite and bless His covenant family.
